title: The Signal Sent Ten Thousand Times: A Fast Sensor, a Queued Connection and a Latest Value That Counts What It Replaced

questions.question: A sensor emits a queued signal 10000 times before the receiving thread's loop runs. How many times does the slot run?
options: Only as many as the queue's default size
10000 times: Qt does not merge queued signals
questions.explanation: Each emit is an event in the queue.

questions.question: Why does publish post a delivery only when one is not already waiting?
options: One waiting delivery will pick up the newest value anyway
Because invokeMethod fails the second time
questions.explanation: More only fill the queue. 10000 writes before the loop were one update.

questions.question: What would happen if deliver forgot to set pending_ to false?
options: The skipped count would be wrong but updates would continue
Every write after the first update would find a delivery 'waiting' that never comes, and the interface would freeze
questions.explanation: The pending flag is cleared by the delivery so the next write posts a new one.

questions.question: What is asserted about 200000 writes from another thread?
options: That updates plus the sum of skipped equal the writes, and the last value arrives
That every write is an update
questions.explanation: The number of updates changes from run to run, the law does not.

questions.question: A lambda connected with no receiver object to a signal emitted from the sensor's thread runs where?
questions.explanation: It is a direct connection. A direct slot runs in the thread that emitted.

questions.question: When is LatestValue the wrong choice?
options: When every reading must be kept, as in a log
When the interface shows a number
questions.explanation: It keeps only the newest and counts the rest: a log wants all of them.
